audit_basis: Phase 3 verification against the live authoritative Cardcom V11 OpenAPI spec (https://secure.cardcom.solutions/swagger/v11/swagger.json, self-reported version 11.0), parsed directly for endpoint paths, schema property names, and enum values; plus WebSearch/WebFetch on Israeli VAT sources and npm/GitHub for community libraries. Removed a fabricated Documents/CreateTaxInvoice endpoint that does not exist in the spec.

claims.claim: Cardcom V11 is the current REST API as of 2026; no public V12 exists.
claims.where_in_skill: SKILL.md Overview, references/api-endpoints.md API Version section
claims.source_note: Probed 2026-07-28: /swagger/v12/swagger.json returns HTTP 404, /swagger/v11/swagger.json returns 200. No public V12.

claims.claim: Production base URL is https://secure.cardcom.solutions/api/v11/
Every V11 endpoint returns ResponseCode (int) and Description (string); ResponseCode == 0 means success.
claims.raw_snippet: "ResponseCode":{"description":"if equal zero then success , 700 and 701 success for J2 and J5 transaction"},"Description":{...} (present on every V11 response schema)

claims.claim: Cardcom supports Bit, PayPal, Apple Pay, and Google Pay as alternative payment methods alongside credit cards.
claims.raw_snippet: אנו מכבדים את כל מותגי האשראי, כולל ביט והארנקים הדיגיטליים - הכל במקום אחד
claims.where_in_skill: SKILL.md Alternative Payment Methods table, Example 5
claims.source_note: Homepage nav also lists 'ביט לעסקים' and 'Apple Pay / Google Pay' as products. PayPal support is evidenced separately by the UrlToPayPal field on CreateLowProfileResponse in the V11 spec (claim 6), not by this page.

claims.claim: Bit payments are returned as a separate UrlToBit field on CreateLowProfileResponse.
PayPal is returned as a separate UrlToPayPal field on CreateLowProfileResponse.
Apple Pay and Google Pay are rendered as wallet buttons inside the hosted Low Profile page itself once enabled on the terminal; no separate URL field exists in the API response.
claims.where_in_skill: SKILL.md Alternative Payment Methods table, Gotchas
claims.source_note: Only Bit and PayPal get their own URL fields. Apple Pay / Google Pay are wallet buttons rendered inside the hosted page (Url), which is why no separate field exists; Cardcom's homepage lists them as supported products.

claims.claim: DocumentTypeToCreate is a string enum (e.g. 'TaxInvoiceAndReceipt'), not an integer code. Integer codes belong to legacy .aspx interfaces.

V11 Document object field spellings: Languge (missing second 'a', on the Document and DocumentTran schemas), ISOCoinID/ISOCoinId, IsSendByEmail, TaxId. The DocumentLP sub-schema (LowProfile flow) uses the correctly-spelled Language, and the LowProfile/Create request carries a top-level Language field.
claims.raw_snippet: "Document":{"properties":{..."Languge"...}},"DocumentTran":{"properties":{..."Languge"...}},"DocumentLP":{"properties":{..."Language"...}} (Languge on Document+DocumentTran; correctly-spelled Language only on DocumentLP)

claims.claim: ApiPassword is required on 19 of the 50 V11 endpoints, including Transactions/ListTransactions and Transactions/SpecialTransactions, not only CreateDocument and RefundByTransactionId. It is not a property at all on LowProfile/Create or Transactions/Transaction.

claims.claim: Israeli VAT rate is 18% as of 2026 (raised from 17% in January 2025; the 2026 budget proposal to raise to 19% was rejected).
claims.raw_snippet: Value-added tax (VAT) The 2025 current rate of VAT is 18%.
claims.source_note: PwC Israel corporate tax summary, page states 'Last reviewed - 29 June 2026'. Replaces vatcalc.com, which returns HTTP 403 to plain fetches.

claims.claim: PCI DSS v4.0.1 is the current standard (limited revision published June 2024); of the 64 new requirements, 51 were future-dated and became effective 31 March 2025.
claims.raw_snippet: Of the 64 new requirements, 51 are future-dated and will be effective as of 31 March 2025. And now, PCI DSS v4.0.1 was released as a limited revision in June 2024

claims.claim: Hosted Low Profile keeps merchants in SAQ-A scope; direct server-to-server Transaction with raw CardNumber/CVV2 falls under SAQ-D.
claims.raw_snippet: Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) A includes only those PCI DSS requirements applicable to merchants with account data functions completely outsourced to PCI DSS validated and compliant third parties, where the merchant retains only paper reports or receipts with account data. ... do not store, process, or transmit any account data in electronic format on their systems or premises.
claims.source_note: SAQ A eligibility turns on NOT storing/processing/transmitting account data, which is what hosted Low Profile achieves and what server-to-server Transaction with raw CardNumber/CVV2 breaks; a merchant handling account data directly falls to SAQ D.

claims.claim: Cardcom supports two recurring-payment flavours: card-based (charge a stored Token) and MASAV bank standing orders (direct bank debit via RecuringPayments endpoints).
claims.raw_snippet: פתרון מתקדם לגבייה מחזורית באשראי או בהוראת קבע בנקאית ... הפעלת הוראת קבע בנקאית דרך מס"ב — ישירות מחשבון הבנק של הלקוח
claims.source_note: 'Credit card charges' + 'Bank standing orders via MASAV'

claims.claim: Cardcom publishes three settlement cycles: monthly (1st to day-before-month-end, credited the 6th of the following month), weekly (Sun-Fri, credited the following Wednesday), and bi-monthly (1st-15th credited the 2nd; 16th-month-end credited the 8th). Configured per terminal, not via API.
claims.raw_snippet: זיכוי חודשי: עסקאות שבוצעו מה-1 לחודש ועד יום לפני סוף החודש – ב-6 לחודש העוקב זיכוי שבועי: עסקאות שבוצעו מיום ראשון עד יום שישי – ביום רביעי בשבוע שאחרי* זיכוי דו-חודשי: עסקאות מה-1 עד ה-15 לחודש – ב-2 לחודש העוקב; עסקאות מה-16 ועד יום לפני סוף החודש – ב-8
claims.source_note: Resolves the 2.2.0 carry item that softened settlement days for lack of a source. Reached via https://www.cardcom.solutions/עמלת-סליקה-לעסקים/ which 301s here.

claims.claim: Cardcom publishes a starting clearing fee of about 1.2% that decreases with transaction volume. This is an advertised floor, not a quote.
claims.raw_snippet: העמלה מתחילה בכ-1.2%, ויכולה לרדת בהתאם למחזור הפעילות שלכם
claims.source_note: Resolves the 2.2.0 carry item on pricing. Deliberately recorded as a floor; the skill still routes users to Cardcom for an actual quote.

claims.claim: Tranzila, Israpay and Bit Business are Israeli payment gateways operating in the same market as Cardcom. Which of them is any given merchant's realistic alternative is not something this skill asserts.
claims.raw_snippet: Tranzila operates a live Israeli payment-gateway service; skills-il additionally ships a dedicated tranzila-payment-gateway skill for it.
claims.source_note: Downgraded from the previous 'main competitors' framing, which was editorial and cited to a crypto-payments marketing blog. The skill only needs the fact that alternatives exist and that Tranzila has its own skill.

claims.claim: RecuringPayments path uses single 'r' spelling in the V11 schema (RecuringPayments, not RecurringPayments).

Terminal 1000 and card 4580000000000000 are widely repeated in community libraries as Cardcom test credentials. NOT confirmed against any official Cardcom sandbox page; the skill presents them as unverified community folklore and warns not to assume terminal 1000 cannot move money.
claims.source_note: UNRESOLVED CARRY. The credentials themselves have no official source. This entry records only that a community package exists; the skill body states plainly that the creds are unverified.

claims.claim: Operation enum values on LowProfile/Create: ChargeOnly (default), ChargeAndCreateToken, CreateTokenOnly, SuspendedDeal, Do3DSAndSubmit.
Cardcom's standout differentiator versus other Israeli gateways is automatic generation of Israeli tax documents (חשבונית מס + קבלה) bundled into the payment flow.
claims.raw_snippet: הלקוח משלם בנוחות, החשבונית מתקבלת אוטומטית והכסף נוחת בחשבון הבנק

claims.claim: Transaction endpoint J2/J5 validation-only operations return ResponseCode 700 or 701 which also count as success.
claims.raw_snippet: "ResponseCode":{"description":"if equal zero then success , 700 and 701 success for J2 and J5 transaction"} (TransactionInfo)

claims.claim: @tsdiapi/cardcom is a community-maintained TypeScript/Node.js client for V11; latest published version is 0.4.0 (2025-11-20). It is third-party and not affiliated with Cardcom.
claims.source_note: Registry API used because the npmjs.com web page returns 403 to plain fetches. Last publish 2025-11-20, so 'actively maintained' is no longer accurate; claim softened to a dated fact.

claims.claim: Suspended deals (Operation SuspendedDeal) return a SuspendedDealId and are charged later via the SuspendedDeals endpoint group, which includes SuspendedDeals/Charge, SuspendedDeals/Cancel, and SuspendedDeals/GetSuspendedDealInfo.

The production endpoint URLs used in the examples all exist in the live V11 OpenAPI spec: https://secure.cardcom.solutions/api/v11/LowProfile/Create, https://secure.cardcom.solutions/api/v11/LowProfile/GetLpResult, https://secure.cardcom.solutions/api/v11/Documents/CreateDocument, https://secure.cardcom.solutions/api/v11/Transactions/Transaction, https://secure.cardcom.solutions/api/v11/Transactions/RefundByTransactionId.
Redirect and webhook URLs in the code samples (example.com/success, /failed, /webhook) are illustrative placeholders, not real Cardcom endpoints.
claims.raw_snippet: Placeholders, not live endpoints: https://example.com/success https://example.com/failed https://example.com/webhook and the sample document link https://secure.cardcom.solutions/doc/10042 (a fixture in scripts/validate_cardcom_response.py matching DocumentNumber 10042, so it 404s by design). IANA: 'example.com and example.org are maintained' as IANA-managed Reserved Domains for documentation. Illustrative amounts in the worked examples, including 149 NIS / 149 שח monthly, are sample figures and not a pricing claim.
claims.source_note: example.com is IANA-reserved for documentation, which is exactly why it is used here.

claims.claim: Cardcom built a direct interface to the Tax Authority so the allocation number is requested automatically when the document is issued, after a one-time setup: identify in the ITA personal area, register the corporation for a company or VAT-registered group, and under 'הרשאות לפעולות דיגיטליות' grant BOTH 'אימות מספר הקצאה בחשבונית ספק' and 'בקשת מספר הקצאה עבור חשבונית ללקוח'. Pre-VAT thresholds: 25,000 (2024), 20,000 (2025), 10,000 (from 1 Jan 2026), 5,000 (from 1 Jun 2026). An osek patur is unaffected.
claims.raw_snippet: קארדקום פיתחה ממשק ישיר מול רשות המיסים, כך שהפעולה תתבצע אוטומטית בעת הפקת המסמך. כדי להפעיל את האוטומציה הזו, יש לבצע הגדרה חד-פעמית ... חובה לבחור בשתי האפשרויות הבאות ... שנת 2024: 25,000 ₪ (25,000 ש"ח / 25,000 NIS) שנת 2025: 20,000 ₪ (20,000 ש"ח / 20,000 NIS) החל מה-1 בינואר 2026: 10,000 ₪ (10,000 ש"ח / 10,000 NIS) החל מה-1 ביוני 2026: 5,000 ₪ (5,000 ש"ח / 5,000 NIS)

claims.claim: The Cardcom OpenAPI spec (title 'CardCom API', version 11.0, 59 paths) contains no allocation-number field: CreateDocumentRequest exposes ApiName, ApiPassword, Document, Cash, Cheques, CustomFields, DealNumbers, IsSendSMS, and DocumentBase's 17 properties include none.
ListTransactionsReq has no TerminalNumber property and sets additionalProperties:false, so sending TerminalNumber fails the call; terminal scoping uses the optional LimitForTerminal.

claims.claim: ListTransactions dates are DDMMYYYY strings; Page starts at 1 and Page_size must be 10-2000.

Transactions/SpecialTransactions is a read endpoint returning other transactions when Cardcom is the acquirer; its only four properties are ApiName, ApiPassword, FromDate, ToDate, all required. It takes no TerminalNumber and no Amount.
